Routes, favourites, monitoring, alerts, widgets and the punctuality history remain on the device. The punctuality history keeps, only on the phone and for up to 90 days, the date, number, operator, delay and cancellation of trains opened with operational data or monitored. A train’s history can be deleted from its Punctuality card, shown from the second observation; deleting the app data removes all of it. Android backup and transfer are excluded; the JSON file is exported only if you choose it. Location is used only to order nearby stations (also when you tap “Nearest” on the station board widget, which keeps only the chosen station) and, if you turn on the GPS alarm, to tell when you are near your stop: it is processed only in memory and is neither retained nor sent to railway sources or anyone else.

Notifications are local reminders. Dictation uses the system recogniser: Binario does not record audio and uses only the returned text. RFI searches send the source the public identifier of the departure station; optional personal sources may receive an identifier or the station name. Without an authorised source: real-time data unavailable. ViaggiaTreno uses HTTP for its public API: station, time and train requests are unencrypted. Other sources use HTTPS.

If you enable the smartwatch, it receives a summary of the route and up to two services. Turning off sharing deletes the DataItem and the watch’s local cache when the revocation is received. The full notice is PRIVACY.md in the repository. A verified URL and privacy contact are still missing before a public release: there is not yet a public link in the app.

Also alert me based on my location

Rings when you are within the chosen radius of the stop (straight away if you already are), even if the train is early or late. If the time-based alarm rings while your position shows the stop is still far away, the GPS alarm stays on.
On high-speed and long-distance trains choose a wider radius: at top speed the train covers several kilometres a minute, so a wider radius gives you time to get ready.

For this alert Binario asks for your precise location and uses it only while the GPS alarm is on, including with the screen off, with an ongoing notification you can stop at any time. Your location is processed only in memory on the phone: it is never stored, logged or sent.
If you grant only approximate location, Android updates it less often: the alert uses a wider radius and may come earlier or later.
The GPS alarm stops by itself on arrival and at the latest two hours after the expected time. After the phone restarts it does not resume on its own: turn it on again from the app.
